$comment: The scaffolder's step order and the tree it produces. Data only: paths, order, and the
few file bodies that are not prose. No handbook text and no instructions live here.
SKILL.md executes these steps in array order and tests/skills/new-project-scaffold.test.mjs
executes them too, so the instructions and the test cannot drift apart.
role is one of observability, repository, product, handbook. 'product' marks product code:
EN-14 requires the observability step to be on disk before every one of them, which is why
logs/ is first in the array and why the test checks for it again at emission time.
A step carrying "authored": true has no "content" key and must never gain one. Its text is
written per project by the agent following SKILL.md. That is what keeps prose out of a data
file, per CLAUDE.md's rule that content artifacts are authored, never templated.
A step carrying "from" takes both its path and its content from the named seed entry,
because both are stack-specific. A step carrying "appendSeed" appends the named seed's
lines to its own content, for the same reason.
seeds holds one entry per stack the scaffolder can write a starting manifest for. Node is
the only entry because node is the one toolchain this plugin already requires (D8), so it
is the one stack a seed can assume is installed. Every other stack is written to its own
conventions by the agent and then confirmed with hooks/stack.mjs, which is the check that
actually guarantees the record resolves to a command at all.
The aeo-tests.json step is the project's record of its own test command (D29, amended by
D30). No gate runs what it names any more; sandbox-guard.mjs reads it to recognise the
project's suite by name, so it is stack-specific and comes from the seed. Whoever writes
the manifest writes the record: for a stack with no seed the agent writes both, and the
command it records is the one it just ran green in step 5.
The .claude/settings.json step (P6.2, issue #64) declares AEO_LIVE_DATA_ROOT and
AEO_DATA_ROOT both blank. sandbox-guard.mjs reads an empty string as not-set and stays
inert until both are filled in, so a blank pair is the safe default rather than an
accidentally-enabled one. It is Claude Code's own settings file, not the project config
file D10 forbids, and it is tracked in git: .gitignore excludes only settings.local.json.
A step carrying "when" is written only when the founder's answers match it: every key
in the object names an entry in "answers", and the answer given must be one of the
values listed. A step with no "when" is always written. That is the whole mechanism,
deliberately: the plan says which files a project gets and the answers decide, with no
expression language to learn or to get wrong. LEDGER.md is the one conditional step
today, because a project where no money moves has no dollars to carry.
A step carrying "requires" names the literal strings its authored text has to contain.
These are not taste. Each one is what a reader under plugin/hooks/ matches on, so a
file that drops its marker leaves the sensorium printing "none declared" for that line
while the file itself still looks written: the status table under a Status heading is
the score (phase 2 decision 3), the **Kill line.** item is the bar (phase 2 decision
4), Ceiling $<n> is where dollars come from (phase 0 decision 2), and the Date /
Recommendation / Executed header is the commitment ledger (phase 0 decision 4).
answers holds the two questions SKILL.md asks before it writes a line. The oracle is
the one project-specific thing (PLAN.md section 2): a key and rubric, an acceptance
suite over samples, the founder as reader with a written checklist, or none yet. A
project that answers "none yet" still gets a status table, so its score prints as
0 of <n> phases done rather than as nothing at all. money decides LEDGER.md, and a
yes carries the ceiling its first line records.
founderDocs (issue #124) is not a step; it is the rule SKILL.md's step 3 applies before
it starts walking the steps array. A founder who writes a PRD, a spec, a research note
or a sketch into the project root before scaffolding gets it filed under destination
rather than left at the root once the scaffold finishes. excludeAtRoot is a fixed list
of names tooling actually reads from a repository root, never a pattern match on a name
like "PRD" — a founder document keeps whatever name it already had.
